text:
Monica Patel: quickstarts repo updates — can we align on what templates to touch first for Phase 1 (Hosted API) + how we keep them in sync w/ docs going forward?

Ibrahim Khan: +1. right now quickstarts are drift city. snippets differ from docs (retry defaults + streaming in TS).

Dana Lo: agree. if we try to update everything at once we’ll never ship. suggest we pick a “golden path” template for each SDK.

Wei Chen: docs side: we’re writing the checklist steps assuming there’s a canonical quickstart per language. i need to know URLs + what repo is source of truth for code.

Elliot Price: also want to avoid duplicating the same explanation in 3 places. ideal: docs can reference “this exact sample” and quickstarts README can link back to docs for narrative.

Monica Patel: proposals for first set:
1) hosted-api / first-request (non-stream)
2) hosted-api / streaming
3) minimal prod readiness (timeouts/retries + request ids)

…for Python/TS/Go.

Ibrahim Khan: for ordering, checklist wants “first request” then “streaming” then “retries/timeouts” (or folded into prod launch doc). so quickstart should mirror that.

Dana Lo: templates in quickstarts repo today:
- /python
- /typescript
- /go
(and a few older ones)
I’d prioritize the ones we send people to from Console: single README path per lang.

Wei Chen: can we please pick *one* folder naming scheme across languages? right now python is “basic-chat”, ts is “streaming-chat”, go is “minimal”. hard to link reliably.

Monica Patel: yeah. if we’re changing structure, now is the time.

Elliot Price: docs IA plan is to deep link to stable URLs like:
/docs/quickstart/python
/docs/quickstart/typescript
/docs/quickstart/go
Those pages can embed code blocks and link to GitHub for full project.

Ibrahim Khan: question: do we want docs snippets to be copied from quickstarts (source) or quickstarts to be generated from docs?

Dana Lo: my vote: code lives in quickstarts repo as runnable projects. docs pulls snippets from there (or we manually copy but enforce w/ CI).

Wei Chen: +1 runnable is key. docs can’t be the only source for code bc it’s not executed.

Elliot Price: ok but we need to solve snippet extraction so writers aren’t copy/pasting. could do “snippet markers” in code + a script to render into docs MD.

Ibrahim Khan: we already have something similar in sdk repos (the docs build pulls examples). can we reuse pattern?

Monica Patel: yes. lightweight approach for Phase 1:
- quickstarts repo becomes canonical
- docs link to quickstarts + include small snippets
- we add a CI check that ensures docs snippets == quickstarts snippets for certain blocks

Dana Lo: what’s the smallest viable CI check? even just “snippets are included from files” rather than inline would help.

Elliot Price: we can do MD includes in docs site if we expose raw GitHub files (or vendor into docs repo at build time). i’ll check with docs build pipeline.

Wei Chen: for Phase 1 copy deadlines: i can tolerate *temporary* manual copy if we have a clear plan to remove it. but we should at least pin commit SHAs so it doesn’t silently drift.

Ibrahim Khan: pinning SHAs seems good. we can add a “Last synced from quickstarts@<sha>” line in docs pages.

Monica Patel: ok. template priority question — which features must be covered?
- first request (chat)
- streaming
- structured output example? (or leave for later)
- embeddings? (probably later)

Dana Lo: structured output is in checklist basics but might be docs-only for now. adding it to quickstarts means more surface + more drift risk.

Wei Chen: checklist step list (current) expects:
- create key
- first request
- streaming basics
- error handling/retries
- rate limits / 429
- usage dashboard / observability
So quickstarts should at minimum have first request + streaming + retries.

Ibrahim Khan: for retries, we need consistent defaults across SDKs. python PR has changes pending (backoff + error typing). TS has some streaming stability changes.

Dana Lo: TS quickstart should also show abort/timeouts. otherwise folks hang forever and call support.

Monica Patel: agreed. keep it minimal:
- explicit timeout
- retry w/ backoff on 429/5xx
- log request id

Wei Chen: please also show the “prod vs test key” header usage / environment variable naming. we keep seeing 401s from using the wrong key.

Ibrahim Khan: can do env var pattern: REDWOOD_API_KEY for local, REDWOOD_API_KEY_PROD for prod example + callout in README.

Dana Lo: or “REDWOOD_API_KEY” + separate .env.example with comments. anything but “API_KEY=xxxx” pls :)

GitHub Bot: PR opened by @dlo: redwood-quickstarts#611 “Add first request + streaming guided steps in README (copy aligns w/ Console checklist)”

Monica Patel: nice. can we also open the “prod readiness” update as separate PR so we can land in smaller chunks?

Dana Lo: yep. i’ll split: #611 for README flow, and another for code changes (timeouts/retries).

Elliot Price: for docs, we have PR draft coming for “First production launch” page. i want to link to quickstarts README sections by anchor. please keep anchors stable (no renaming headings every day).

Wei Chen: +1. also: please don’t use “Getting started” as every heading. makes anchor collisions.

Ibrahim Khan: action items i’m hearing:
1) pick canonical templates: python/typescript/go under /hosted-api (single folder) (owner: Monica + Dana)
2) update “first request” + “streaming” steps and ensure code compiles (owner: Dana w/ review from Ibrahim)
3) add retries/timeouts + request id logging (owner: Ibrahim)
4) docs pages link to quickstarts w/ pinned SHA + “last synced” note (owner: Elliot + Wei)
5) follow-up: snippet extraction / CI to keep in sync (owner: Elliot, but needs eng help)

Monica Patel: yep. and sequencing: land runnable quickstarts first, then docs deep links.

Elliot Price: works. i’ll update writers: assume quickstarts are canonical; docs will pin SHA for beta.

Wei Chen: timeline: need final quickstart paths by end of week to wire Console links.

Dana Lo: i can get folder restructure + README updates in by Thu. code changes for retries/timeouts by Mon (pending SDK changes).

Ibrahim Khan: i’ll sync w/ python/go owners to make sure our retry guidance matches SDK behavior. don’t want a quickstart promising retries the SDK doesn’t do.

Monica Patel: great. pls drop links here when PRs are up + we’ll get reviews queued. :thumbsup:

Dana Lo: will do.

Elliot Price: thanks all. keep me posted on final folder names so i can lock doc URLs + avoid redirects later.

Wei Chen: +1 (redirects are pain).
